items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: such as you and Stanley Dance, Leonard Feather

ctx.x: I had ever heard, and of course, Sid Catlett and Dave were considered the tops of their times.

Bear in mind that Dave Tough influenced people like the so-called modern drummers. Now, we in jazz, we musicians in jazz do not use categories. We do not put people into categories and I will go into that in a few minutes. We don't call a man a modern drummer or an avant garde drummer or a dixieland drummer. A man can either play or he cannot. This is what it's about and only musicians know this. Not critics, I am sorry to say, with the exception perhaps of a few, such as you and Stanley Dance, Leonard Feather.…

Say that musicians never called the music jazz, but they knew what they were hearing and what they were feeling. It was the only kind of music they could find wherein they could express their feelings, because they worked all day in studios or theatres and all night in night- clubs, playing dance music or playing other people's acts, but why did they want to play this kind of music? Because they had a chance to express what they felt about music.
